subject: tech
title: When This Happens: Events
about: An event is something that happens and starts a program: a tap plays a sound, a shake changes the picture, the alarm time makes the alarm ring (K2-AP-05, K2-AP-01). The cards ask what started it, what happened because of it, how a program waits for an event, and how two different events make two different things happen. Events are a bridge topic, taught from Grade 3 on, so read it together and point out the real-life events all day: the doorbell rings, you open the door.
tip: Play what started it: every time something beeps, rings or lights up today, ask him to name the event and then the action.

cards.q: Something that happens and starts a program, like a tap on a button, has a name. What is it?
cards.note: An event is a happening the program waits for: a tap, a shake, a clap, a time.

cards.q: When the button is tapped, the sound plays. What is the event?
cards.note: The event is the thing that happens first and starts everything else.

cards.q: When the button is tapped, the sound plays. What happens because of the event?
cards.note: Event first, then the action. The tap starts it, the sound is what happens.

cards.q: When you shake the tablet, the picture changes. What started the change?
cards.note: A tablet can feel a shake. The shake is the event that starts the change.

cards.q: When the alarm time comes, the alarm rings. What is the event here?
cards.note: Time can be an event too. The clock reaching seven is what starts the ring.

cards.q: When you clap, the robot turns. What is the event?
cards.note: The robot's microphone hears the clap. That sound is the event.

cards.q: The doorbell rings and you open the door. Which part is the event?
cards.note: Life is full of events. The ring happens, then you act.

cards.q: The phone rings and Grandma answers it. What happens because of the ring?
cards.note: The ring is the event. Answering is the action it starts.

cards.q: A program has one button. Nobody has tapped it yet. What is the program doing?
cards.note: A program can wait and wait. The moment the event happens, it acts.

cards.q: Tap the drum: boom. Tap the bell: ding. You tap the bell. What do you hear?
cards.note: Two events, two actions. Each tap starts its own sound.

cards.q: Tap the drum: boom. Tap the bell: ding. You tap the drum. What happens?
cards.note: The drum tap is a different event, so a different sound plays.

cards.q: In a game, which event would make the character jump?
cards.note: Match the event to the action. A tap on the jump button makes a jump.

cards.q: A night light turns on when the room gets dark. What starts the light?
cards.note: Getting dark is the event. Turning on is the action.

cards.q: Brushing your teeth is a list of steps. A tap that starts a game is what?
cards.note: Steps are what to do. An event is what starts it.

cards.q: You want the picture to change when the tablet is shaken. Which event do you pick?
cards.note: Pick the event, then the action: when shake, change the picture.

cards.q: You tilt the tablet and the ball rolls. What started the roll?
cards.note: A tablet can feel a tilt. The tilt is the event that starts the rolling.

cards.q: A game waits for a tap, a shake and a swipe. How many different events is that?
cards.note: Tap, shake, swipe: three events. Each one can start its own action.

cards.q: The microwave beeps and you take out the popcorn. What was the event?
cards.note: The beep happens, then you act. The beep is the event.
